newsitem.title: DUBAI: International waters near Bakr seen clear of mines.
newsitem.headline: International waters near Bakr seen clear of mines.

text.p: The international waters around Iraq's Mina al-Bakr port appeared to be clear of mines laid during the 1990-91 Gulf War, Gulf shipping sources said on Tuesday.
"As far as I know there are no problems," one said, adding that the main waterway into Mina al-Bakr had been swept of mines left from the both the 1990-91 war and the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war.
"The waterway into al-Bakr from the Gulf is clear," said another.
A U.S. naval official said the navy was comfortable operating its ships in the international waters.
"The U.S. navy has ships operating up the coast of that area routinely...and over the years we have become more comfortable about operating in that area in the international waters," he said.
But some shipping firms still are concerned about debris and mines around the offshore loading terminal at Mina al-Bakr -- Iraq's main export point for crude oil shipments to Asia.
